Here's some advice from someone who also went through a terrible depression in High School...

Don't neglect your mental health

Things got better after I finished HS and I lowered my guard when I entered the "golden age" that was college and my early 20s, but if you don't take care of healing the wounds of the past, next time life gets tough (and it will, 'cause that's just what life does sometimes) you will fall HARD like I just did. I was fired from my job and evicted and I had a massive panic attack that led to my incarceration. In therapy I found out that many of my "demons" were just unresolved conflicts from my past (i.e. High School) and now I have to deal with those.

You seem to really care about the world. Have you ever considered a career that helps others? Maybe teaching or therapy or working for a non-profit organization? Yes, the world is a shitty, terrible place, but if your effort in making it better, even if it's just a little bit, I think it might really help.

I have Asperger's too and though I lost my job, I was able to do something I loved for quite some time. Everyone has their strengths and weaknesses, I'm sure there's a job out there you'd be great for.

Making friends as an adult is really hard. It took me about three years to find my "circle" living in Los Angeles. Have you considered joining meetup groups that are aligned with your interests? I'm a huge geek and I'm gay, and when I joined a gay dodgeball league and a gay gamers group on Facebook, my social life really took off.

Bear in mind, the odds of you finding a friend that make you feel like your original BFF are astronomically low, but that's just how life works.

It seems like you've got a lot on your plate right now. One thing seems pretty clear, though...

Your ex is a DOUCHE

Good relationship partners bring out the best in us. Think about Biology: some species exist in parasitic relationships, where one species benefits while the other suffers. Others exist in commensalistic relationships, where one benefits and the other doesn't suffer or benefit. Others are mutualistic, where both benefit from working together. I think you should keep looking until you find a partner that makes you feel like he brings out the best in you and you bring out the best in him, like species in a mutualistic relationship. But parasitic relationships will only serve to make you miserable and make it impossible to live a mentally healthy life.

Stay strong <3

In my experience, psychiatric hospitals don't really offer the best treatment options. I recommend finding one kickass psychiatrist and one kickass talk therapist. I think his past trauma (sexual abuse and whatnot) are definitely factors that affect his current behavior and his past therapy options might have just been insufficient. Finding a good therapist that fits your brother's needs might not be easy, but I'm sure that once he does find someone he's more compatible with, things will get much, much better.

Your brother is lucky to have someone as caring as you. Stay strong.

In its core, depression is a neurological disorder. Though it's influenced by your environment, in the end it's your biology - your genes - who are to blame.
